# Ledgerline

An expense tracker built from the Claude Design canvas of the same name —
Express + MongoDB Atlas on the back, React + Vite on the front. A public
marketing home page, accounts with sign-up and sign-in, and a dashboard where
every number is computed from the database; nothing is hard-coded.

```
server/   Express API, Mongoose models, seed script
client/   React app (Vite), Nocturne design system
```

## Getting started

```bash
npm run install:all     # root + server + client dependencies
npm run dev             # API on :4000, client on :5173
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` to port 4000.

Register from the home page and you get five starter categories to work with.
To look around a full month instead, run `npm run seed` and sign in as:

```
demo@ledgerline.app / demo1234
```

For a single-origin run, build the client and let Express serve it:

```bash
npm run build
npm start               # everything on http://localhost:4000
```

### Configuration

`server/.env` (already filled in; see `.env.example`):

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `MONGODB_URI` | MongoDB Atlas connection string |
| `PORT` | API port, default `4000` |
| `CLIENT_ORIGIN` | Allowed CORS origin(s), comma-separated |
| `JWT_SECRET` | Signing key for session tokens — generated for you; rotate it and everyone is signed out |
| `JWT_EXPIRES` | Session lifetime, default `30d` |

## Screens

Public:

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Home — a scroll-driven particle field morphing through five chapters |
| `/login` · `/register` | Sign in / create an account |

The dashboard, all of it behind sign-in:

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/app` | Overview — four stat tiles, six-month trend, category split, recent activity |
| `/app/expenses` | Filter by segment and category, search notes; paginated; CSV export |
| `/app/expenses/new` | Add an expense — amount, date, category, note |
| `/app/expenses/:id` | Detail — edit, duplicate, split, delete, plus an audit history |
| `/app/expenses/:id/edit` | The add form in edit mode |
| `/app/budgets` | Envelope ring, per-category pace, inline budget editing |
| `/app/reports` | Trend (bars/area/dots), category donut, daily rhythm, movers vs last month |
| `/app/categories` | Cards with counts and auto-sort rules; create, edit, delete |
| `/app/settings` | Currency, period start, monthly budget, rounding, reminders, export |

The month stepper in the header drives every dashboard screen at once. Visiting
an `/app` route while signed out sends you to `/login` and then on to where you
were headed.

### The home page

`Home.jsx` plus `lib/particles.js` — a faithful port of the supplied
`expense-tracker-particle-morph.html` reference: a scroll-driven WebGL particle
field behind five chapters of copy.

One swarm of 1,400 points is reused for five formations and morphed between them
by scroll position — a chaotic cloud, six category clusters, a bar chart, an
ascending trendline, and a launch arrow. Shapes, colours, point size, camera
path, easing and keyframes are the reference's values, unchanged.

Two details are load-bearing and easy to "improve" by mistake:

- **The material is untextured.** `PointsMaterial` with no `map` renders each
  point as a crisp square, which is the look. Giving it a radial sprite softens
  every point into a blur and loses it.
- **The camera makes a full turntable sweep** (`progress * π * 1.3`). Swinging
  it to face the formations head-on reads better in isolation but is not the
  reference's motion.

The landing page carries the reference's own palette (`#0A0B14` ink, `#6C7CFF`
indigo, `#FF7A59` coral) and type (Space Grotesk, IBM Plex Mono), all scoped
under `.lp` so none of it leaks into the Nocturne-styled dashboard.

Deviations from the reference, all deliberate:

- **three.js is dynamically imported**, so it lands in its own ~512 KB chunk.
  Anyone going straight to `/app` never downloads it; the dashboard bundle stays
  at ~234 KB.
- **The buttons are real links** — "Start tracking free" goes to `/register`,
  "Sign in" to `/login` (the reference's second button was "See how it works",
  which had nowhere to go). A signed-in visitor gets "Open your dashboard".
- **The product name is Ledgerline**, not the reference's ExpenseFlow.
- **Everything the field creates it disposes**, so React StrictMode's
  double-mount and route changes leave no orphaned canvas or leaked GPU buffers.

> **The three figures in the stat strip — 4.2M+ transactions, 98%
> auto-categorized, 0.3s sync — are placeholders carried over from the reference
> design. They are not measurements of anything.** Replace them before this page
> is public.

## API

All routes are under `/api`. Month parameters take `YYYY-MM`.

**Auth** — `POST /auth/register`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/logout`,
`GET /auth/me`. Passwords are bcrypt-hashed (cost 12) and the hash is
`select: false`, so it never rides along in a query result. The session is a JWT
in an httpOnly, sameSite=lax cookie — page scripts cannot read it, so an XSS bug
cannot walk off with it. Register and login return the same message for a wrong
password as for an unknown address, so neither can be used to discover which
emails have accounts.

Everything below requires that cookie.

**Expenses**

| Method | Route | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/expenses` | `month`, `filter`, `category`, `q`, `page`, `limit`, `sort`, `minAmount`, `maxAmount`. `filter` is `all` / `uncategorized`. `q` matches the note and tags. Returns the page plus `total`, `totalAmount` and `spendAmount`. |
| `GET` | `/expenses/:id` | |
| `POST` | `/expenses` | Needs an amount above zero; everything else is optional. Auto-assigns a category when the note matches a category's keywords. |
| `PATCH` | `/expenses/:id` | Records what changed in the expense's history. |
| `DELETE` | `/expenses/:id` | |
| `POST` | `/expenses/:id/duplicate` | Copies it to today. |
| `POST` | `/expenses/:id/split` | `{ parts: [{ amount, category, note }] }` — parts must total the original. |

**Categories** — `GET/POST /categories`, `PATCH/DELETE /categories/:id`.
Deleting a category leaves its expenses in place as uncategorized.

**Budgets** — `GET /budgets?month=` returns each envelope plus the overall
summary (spend, pace, projection). `PUT /budgets` upserts a whole month.

**Reports** — `/reports/overview`, `/reports/trend`, `/reports/daily`,
`/reports/mix`, `/reports/movers`.

**Settings** — `GET`/`PUT /settings`.

## Data model

- **User** — name, email (unique), bcrypt hash, last login.
- **Expense** — owner, date, amount, category, note, tags, history, `splitFrom`.
  Amount is the only thing required; a row is identified in lists by its
  category and note.
- **Category** — owner, name, icon, colour index, auto-sort keywords,
  `excludeFromSpend`. Unique on `(user, name)`.
- **Budget** — one limit per category per month, unique on `(user, month, category)`.
- **Settings** — one document per account: currency, period start, monthly
  budget, rounding, reminder toggles.

### Four conventions worth knowing

**Every row belongs to an account.** `Expense`, `Category`, `Budget` and
`Settings` all carry a `user`, `requireAuth` puts the owner on `req.userId`, and
every query in every data route filters by it — reads, writes, aggregates and
`findOne` lookups by id alike. Ids supplied by the caller (a category on an
expense, the parts of a split) are checked for ownership before use, so one
account cannot attach itself to another's records. Uniqueness is per account,
not global: two people can both have a category called Transport.

**Keyword rules read the note.** A category's keywords are matched against a
new expense's note, since that is the only free text an expense carries. Leave
the category blank on the form and a note mentioning "grocer" files itself.

**Savings are tracked but not spent.** A category with `excludeFromSpend` still
lists its expenses, but stays out of spend totals, the trend and the budget
ring — so a monthly transfer to savings doesn't read as spending.

**The month is not always the calendar month.** `monthStartsOn` in settings
shifts every period, aggregate and budget window; set it to 25 and August runs
25 Aug → 25 Sep. All the date maths is in `server/src/lib/period.js` and runs in
UTC so the boundaries don't drift with the host timezone.

## Managing the data

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run reset` | Empties everything — expenses, categories, budgets and settings. |
| `npm run seed` | Rebuilds the demo account only. Other accounts are untouched. |

**Both are destructive and neither asks for confirmation.** `reset` wipes
everything including user accounts; `seed` only rebuilds `demo@ledgerline.app`.

`npm run seed` writes 202 expenses across March–August 2026, eight categories and
48 budget envelopes; August comes to ৳48,320 of a ৳60,000 budget across 42
expenses, which is what the original design mocked up. The shop names from the
original design survive as notes on the rows that had no other description. Use it to explore the
app, then `npm run reset` to get back to a clean workspace.

After a reset there are no accounts, so register again from the home page. A new
account gets five starter categories and a settings document built from the
defaults in `models/Settings.js` (BDT, ৳60,000/month, period starting on the 1st).

The server runs `syncIndexes` on boot, which is what drops indexes left behind
by an older schema. The single-user version made `Category.name` and
`Settings.key` globally unique; left in place, those would reject the second
account that created a category named Transport, or tried to register at all.

## Not wired up

- **Receipts.** Removed — an expense holds no image. Bring them back and the
  detail screen needs a panel again, along with a "needs receipt" filter.
- **Merchant, payment method and repeats-monthly.** Also removed. An expense is
  an amount, a date, a category and a note; the note is what labels it in a
  list. Nothing recurs on its own — a monthly bill is entered each month.
- **Bank sync.** The button is present and disabled.
- **Reminders.** The toggles persist; nothing sends mail or notifications.
- **Password reset.** There is no "forgot password" flow, and no email is sent
  anywhere. A lost password means a lost account.
- **Rate limiting.** Nothing throttles repeated login attempts. Worth adding
  before this faces the internet.
